meta.title: Carrie the Swiss · Read the papers before you buy the puppy
meta.description: An animated series hosted by Carrie, a real Greater Swiss Mountain Dog from Slovakia. Pedigrees, health tests, dog shows and responsible breeding, explained with checked facts.

hero.ch1_text: A Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, a show dog, and the host of a series about what people should know before they buy a puppy.

guide.eyebrow: What didn't fit in the video
guide.title: What my papers actually mean.
guide.intro: The longer version of each topic, with sources. Rules differ by country and breed club, so always ask yours.
guide.a1_lead: HD-A, ED-0, OCD-free. What the letters next to a puppy's parents mean.
guide.a1_p1: These joint problems are partly inherited, which is why good breeders X-ray both parents. Great scores lower the risk; they don't erase it. Fast growth and extra weight still count.
guide.a1_p2: A to E is the FCI scale used in Europe. In the US the OFA grades hips from Excellent to Severe, and in the UK the BVA/KC scheme gives a hip score. Ask which scale the papers use.
guide.a2_title: A pedigree is not the whole story
guide.a2_lead: It proves who a puppy comes from, not how it was raised.
guide.a2_p1: The FCI says it itself: a pedigree certifies parentage, not quality. A sunny living room with a mom you can meet, or a garage where the mom is "not available": both puppies can get the same paper.
guide.a2_p2: Check instead: both parents' health results on paper, the mom at the breeder's home with her puppies, and a breeder who asks you questions.
guide.a2_p3: The FCI doesn't issue pedigrees. Your national kennel club does. In Slovakia that's the SKJ, from the Slovak studbook (SPKP).
guide.a3_lead: Once in a dog's life, a committee decides if it may have puppies.
guide.a3_p1: To get in (Slovakia): X-rays of hips (A to C), elbows (0 to 1) and shoulders (clear), a CAC from two dog shows, and at least 15 months of age (18 for males).
guide.a3_p2: Character: seven tasks worth 2, 1 or 0 points each, from walking on the lead and a stranger taking the leash to wobbly ground, loud music and a distant bang. 11 points or more is excellent.
guide.a3_p3: Body: measurements against the standard (females 60 to 68 cm at the withers), bite and teeth, eye colour, build and temperament. When a breeder says a dog passed, ask to see the card.
guide.a4_title: How a responsible litter is planned
guide.a4_lead: Step one isn't finding a boyfriend.
guide.a4_p1: The mom is old enough, healthy and approved for breeding. The dad is not the closest one but the best match: healthy, good-natured and strong where she is weaker.
guide.a4_p2: Breeders check how related the pair is (the inbreeding coefficient, COI). The FCI recommends that no dog should have more offspring than 5% of the puppies registered in the breed over five years.
guide.a4_p3: Progesterone tests find the fertile days, and pregnancy takes about 63 days. Good breeders often have families waiting, and take a dog back at any age.

quote.text: Pedigree says who. X-rays say how healthy. The judge says how close to the blueprint. A good breeder shows you all three.
quote.why: We make these videos for free, so more people know what the papers mean before they bring a puppy home.

quiz.title: Is a Swissy right for you?
quiz.intro: Five honest questions from me. No wrong answers, just useful ones.
quiz.q1: How much space do you have?
quiz.q1b: A house with a small garden
quiz.q1c: Lots of space and fields nearby
quiz.q2: How much time can you spend outside with me every day?
quiz.q2c: Two hours or more, rain or shine
quiz.q3: How do you feel about dog hair?
quiz.q4: An adult Swissy can weigh 40 to 60 kg. Can you handle that?
quiz.q5: We grow up slowly and stay puppies at heart for about three years. Patience?
quiz.r1_title: Maybe not a Swissy. And that's okay.
quiz.r1_text: Honest answer: a smaller or calmer breed might make you both happier. Choosing the right dog is a good decision too.
quiz.r2_title: It could work, with a plan.
quiz.r2_text: Meet adult Swissies, talk to a few breeders and plan the training before the puppy comes home.
quiz.r3_title: You might be my kind of human.
quiz.r3_text: Next step: find a breeder who shows you all the papers. Season one tells you what to look for.
